parsed.thesis: Owner approval is not a starting point for free interpretation—it is an anchor of verified intent. Once an owner approves an artifact version, that state becomes an immutable baseline; every subsequent change is merely a hypothesis that must name its optimization dimension, remain reversible, and prove non-regression against the frozen baseline through observable comparison before it earns a place in the artifact's history. Without this anchor, vague 'make it better' requests invite subjective drift, degradations stack silently, and the agent's sense of 'completed improvement' diverges ever further from the owner's actual preference.

principleCandidate.title: Anchor on approved baselines: keep changes only if verified non-regressive against them
principleCandidate.rationale: The root cause of the pain was unbounded subjective drift: after the owner approved a version, ambiguous optimization requests were self-interpreted as license for free-form changes, each declared successful on 'modification completed' alone. Freezing the approved version as a baseline converts 'improvement' from a subjective judgment into a falsifiable claim—a change is kept only if an observable comparison against the baseline (screenshots, diffs, dimension-by-dimension checks) shows no regression on owner-relevant dimensions. This single anchor also forces clarification of vague goals (what dimension to improve), motivates version isolation for reversibility, and makes small isolated steps the natural unit of verification, addressing all five candidate failure modes coherently.
principleCandidate.scope: Applies whenever an owner or authoritative party has explicitly approved or accepted a version of an artifact (media, documents, code, configurations, plans, generated outputs) and subsequent modification requests—especially vague ones like 'optimize', 'polish', or 'make it better'—arrive. Most critical in iterative editing/generation loops where per-step degradation is easy to miss and changes overwrite prior state. Not applicable when no approved reference exists or when the owner explicitly requests exploratory divergence from prior work.

risks: Overlaps with T-02 (clarify vague goals), T-03/T-07 (observable verification before claiming results), and T-04 (reversible actions); the genuinely new element is only the frozen owner-approved state as the mandatory comparison anchor, and the composite framing risks redundancy with existing axioms if that distinction is lost.

Baseline rigidity: freezing an approved version may block legitimate evolution of owner intent; without an explicit re-approval path to update the baseline, the principle degenerates into change aversion and stalls necessary rework.

Non-regression is ill-defined for subjective quality dimensions (aesthetics, pacing, tone); comparison evidence can be contested, and the gate may devolve into disputes over what counts as degradation.

Clarification overhead: demanding explicit optimization dimensions and acceptance criteria for every minor tweak can slow iteration and frustrate owners who expect fast, low-stakes adjustments; the principle must be applied proportionally to the stakes of the change.

principleDraft.title: Anchor on owner-approved baselines; keep only verified non-regressive changes
principleDraft.statement: When an owner or authoritative party has explicitly approved a version of an artifact, freeze that version as the immutable comparison baseline before applying any subsequent modification. Treat every follow-up change request—especially vague ones like 'optimize', 'polish', or 'make it better'—as a hypothesis that must: (a) name the specific optimization dimension it targets, clarifying with the owner if the dimension is ambiguous; (b) be applied as an isolated, reversible step that preserves the baseline intact; and (c) be retained only after an observable comparison against the baseline (diff, screenshot, dimension-by-dimension check) shows improvement on the targeted dimension and no regression on owner-relevant dimensions. Update the baseline only through explicit owner re-approval, and scale the rigor of this gate proportionally to the stakes of the change.
principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause is unbounded subjective drift: after approval, ambiguous improvement requests were self-interpreted as license for free-form changes, each declared successful on 'modification completed' alone, so silent degradations stacked while the agent's notion of 'improved' diverged from the owner's actual preference. Freezing the approved version as a comparison anchor converts 'improvement' from a subjective judgment into a falsifiable claim—kept only if observable evidence against the baseline shows non-regression. This single anchor also forces the vague goal to be resolved into a named dimension, makes reversibility a structural requirement rather than an afterthought, and makes small isolated steps the natural unit of verification.
applicability: Iterative editing or generation loops where an owner has explicitly approved or accepted a prior version of an artifact (media, documents, code, configurations, plans, generated outputs)
Vague follow-up modification requests such as 'optimize', 'polish', or 'make it better' directed at previously approved work
Environments where changes overwrite prior state and per-step degradation is easy to miss
Boundary: not applicable when no approved reference version exists, or when the owner explicitly requests exploratory divergence from prior work
antiPatterns: Treating owner approval as a starting point for free-form reinterpretation of vague improvement requests
Declaring a change successful based solely on 'modification completed' without an observable comparison against the approved baseline
Overwriting or discarding the approved baseline before the replacement has been verified non-regressive
Accepting regressions on untargeted dimensions as tolerable side effects without explicit owner sign-off
Proceeding to modify without naming the optimization dimension because the request was vague
Freezing the baseline with no re-approval path, turning the anchor into change aversion that blocks legitimate evolution of owner intent

intentContract.ownerIntent: Once the Owner has approved a version, they want every subsequent vague 'improve it' request handled as a targeted, reversible change that is kept only when shown to improve the requested dimension without regressing the approved version—never as license for free-form rework.
intentContract.targetBehavior: Before applying a follow-up change, the agent preserves the owner-approved version as a baseline (copy, version pin, or checkpoint), states which dimension the change optimizes, applies the change reversibly, and then produces a concrete comparison artifact against the baseline (diff, screenshot, or dimension-by-dimension checklist) demonstrating improvement on the target dimension and no regression elsewhere, claiming success only after that comparison.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Treating an approved version as a mere starting point and freely reworking the artifact under vague improvement requests—declaring success from modification completion alone, with no named optimization dimension, no preserved baseline, no observable non-regression comparison, and overwriting the approved state in the process.
intentContract.evidenceSource: Diagnosed pain: after owner approval, vague optimization requests were self-interpreted as license for subjective drift; each change was declared successful on 'modification completed' alone, per-step degradations stacked silently, and the agent's sense of completed improvement diverged from the owner's actual preference.
intentContract.validationExpectation: An evaluator should require, in the trajectory or rule evidence: (1) a preserved baseline reference to the approved version existing before the change, (2) an explicit statement of the targeted optimization dimension, (3) a concrete comparison artifact against the baseline, and (4) success claimed only after that comparison. Rules that merely restate 'verify results' (T-03/T-07) or 'clarify goals' (T-02) without the frozen-baseline anchor and re-approval path should be rejected as unfaithful to this intent.

risks: Overlap with existing core axioms: the clarification requirement echoes T-02, observable verification echoes T-03/T-07, reversibility echoes T-04, and minimal-change framing echoes T-06. The genuinely new element is only the frozen owner-approved baseline as the mandatory comparison anchor plus the explicit re-approval path; if rule generation loses that distinction, the principle degenerates into redundant restatements of existing axioms.
Baseline rigidity: without the explicit re-approval path, freezing the approved version can block legitimate evolution of owner intent and produce change aversion that stalls necessary rework.

Non-regression is ill-defined for subjective quality dimensions (aesthetics, pacing, tone); comparison evidence can be contested and the gate may devolve into disputes over what counts as degradation.

Clarification overhead: demanding a named optimization dimension and comparison evidence for every minor tweak can slow iteration and frustrate owners expecting fast, low-stakes adjustments; application must be proportional to stakes.

Ritualized compliance: the agent may produce token comparison artifacts (e.g., a trivial diff) and still declare success, satisfying the letter of the gate without verifying owner-relevant dimensions.

Environmental dependency: preserving baselines requires snapshot/versioning capability; in environments lacking it, the principle's reversibility requirement may be impractical without workaround tooling.

principleDraft.statement: When the owner has explicitly approved or accepted a version of an artifact, freeze that version as the immutable baseline (recorded by path or content fingerprint, never overwritten) before any further modification. principleDraft.rationale: The diagnosed root cause was unbounded subjective drift: after the owner approved mooncake-mv-final-v3k22.mp4, ambiguous 'optimization' requests were self-interpreted as license for free-form changes, each round accepted on 'modification completed' alone, so degradations stacked silently until the owner corrected: '后面的所谓的优化都没有 mooncake-mv-final-v3k22.mp4 版本好，越搞越乱'. Freezing the approved version as the comparison anchor converts 'improvement' from a subjective self-judgment into a falsifiable non-regression claim—the owner's accepted state is the only legitimate reference for what counts as better or worse, and it survives as the fallback whenever a change cannot prove itself. Existing axioms cover verification (T-03/T-07), intent (T-02), reversibility (T-04) and forbidden degrading transitions (T-05) generically; what they lack is this specific mechanism: the owner-approved artifact as a frozen anchor and mandatory retention gate.
applicability: Iterative editing or generation loops over media, documents, code, configurations, plans, or generated outputs where the owner has explicitly approved or accepted a specific version and further modification requests arrive (especially vague ones: '优化', '改进', 'improve', 'polish', 'make it better')

Not applicable when no owner-approved reference exists yet, or when the owner explicitly requests exploratory divergence from prior work
antiPatterns: Treating owner approval of a version as a starting point for free-form, self-judged 'optimization' without freezing that version as the comparison baseline

Keeping or stacking changes that degrade owner-relevant dimensions relative to the approved baseline
Overwriting or discarding the approved version, making degradation irreversible and reverting impossible
Interpreting vague 'better/optimize' requests as license for self-chosen multi-dimensional changes without naming or confirming the targeted optimization dimension

intentContract.targetBehavior: On any modification request following an owner-approved version, the agent visibly records that version as an immutable baseline (path/fingerprint), applies changes to a separate new version, produces observable comparison evidence against the baseline (e.g., key-frame screenshots, diffs), and reverts unless the comparison shows no regression on owner-relevant dimensions.
intentContract.forbiddenBehavior: Unanchored, self-judged improvement loops after owner approval: modifying without a frozen baseline reference, claiming success from completion alone, keeping or stacking degrading changes, and overwriting the approved version so regression becomes irreversible.
